items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Branford and Harry [Connick], Jr., came here and was wading through all that water.

ctx.x: How did you become associated with the center?

Branford and Harry [Connick], Jr., came here and was wading through all that water. When they saw the damage, the two of them started to talk and said, there’s got to be something we can do. So they started to think about establishing a center. The Musicians’ Village was already underway here, because the Habitat had been building houses down there for a long time. The Musicians’ Village was already there. I think that the property came from the school board. I think there was a school there before it. The…
I think we did. Maybe it just wasn’t identified, the site.

items.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020
items.q: Ellis taught extensively at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts and helped launch the careers of Harry Connick Jr., Terrance Blanchard and Nicholas Payton.

ctx.x: Pianist and educator Ellis Marsalis was born in New Orleans in 1934. He has performed and recorded with a diverse list of artists, including Al Hirt, Cannonball Adderley and Kermit Ruffins. Ellis taught extensively at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts and helped launch the careers of Harry Connick Jr., Terrance Blanchard and Nicholas Payton. He has recorded as a leader and with his sons, Wynton, Branford, Delfeayo and Jason.
Ellis was interviewed in New Orleans, Louisiana on January 7, 2020 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
